r0.why: Ordered basis, unique representation by n scalars called coordinates, coordinate vector: all in [1].

r1.why: 'The simplest case is F^n' adds an evaluative qualifier ('simplest') that [21]-[22] do not give; rest matches.

r2.why: Different coordinate vectors per basis [2], rewriting assertions [3], transition matrix with new basis coordinates on old basis as columns [5].

r3.why: Basis iff A invertible / nonzero determinant [12]; then called change-of-basis matrix from old to new [13].

r4.why: x = Ay gives old in terms of new, may seem unnatural, f(Ay) with no matrix inversion: [29],[30].

r5.why: Orthonormal basis as rotation in physics/mechanics [7]; symmetric bilinear forms in quadrics, rigid body inertia [44]; preference for orthogonal P [45].
